messages.subject: correlation matrix as input
parts:
Hello,

I'm using R for my meta analysis and want to estimate a structural equation model. Unfortunately I do only have a correlation matrix and no standard deviations to estimate covariances. Can I use lavaan anyway? Is there a trick how I can estimate my model?

Thank you for your support,
Fabian

> equation model. Unfortunately I do only have a correlation matrix and no
> standard deviations to estimate covariances. Can I use lavaan anyway? Is
> there a trick how I can estimate my model?

I'm afraid you can not use lavaan (0.5-12) for this. But have a look at
the metaSEM package (which depends on openMx).

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: correlation matrix as input
parts:
On 04/22/2014 10:26 PM, Kai Horstmann wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I did have the same problem - however, I did just use a correlation
> matrix and was also perfectly able to reproduce results from a book with
> it. Has the issue been solved within the last year or do I oversee
> something important?

There are two potential issues:

1) if in a meta analysis, you need to treat the studies as random (as
opposed to fixed), lavaan (0.5) can not handle this

2) if you have a correlation matrix as input (instead of a covariance
matrix), and your model is not 'scale-invariant', you may get the wrong
results. You can still do this with lavaan, but it involves a set of
nonlinear constraints. See eg:

Steiger, J.H. (2002). When constraints interact: A caution about
reference variables, identification constraints, and scale dependencies
in structural equation modeling. Pychological Methods, 7, 210-227.

Yves.
